resolution_rule: Use the first U.S. Department of Labor weekly unemployment-insurance release published 2026-08-27. Resolve the joint event TRUE only if seasonally adjusted initial claims for the week ending 2026-08-22 are below 220,000 AND seasonally adjusted continuing claims for the week ending 2026-08-15 are at least 1,800,000. Otherwise resolve FALSE. Score the 0.57 joint probability by Brier and log loss. Score the two point estimates separately by absolute error versus the same first-release values, compare each against frozen no-change and published-calendar point benchmarks, and record each 80% interval hit. Do not substitute later revisions unless DOL corrects the initial release before scoring.
rationale: The Aug. 20 release showed low separations at 206,000 initial claims but continuing claims at 1.799 million, consistent with the newly separated low-fire / slower-reemployment pathway.
The Aug. 21 services PMI and hiring strength argue against an imminent layoff wave, keeping the <220,000 initial-claims leg more likely than not.

Continuing claims have remained stickier than initial claims and the external calendar point forecast is 1.811 million, so the >=1.800 million continuing-claims leg directly tests whether weak re-employment can coexist with low layoffs.
A joint event is used rather than two highly correlated headline forecasts to avoid inflating sample size while still testing the causal split introduced in v0.2.7.
surprising_if: Initial claims are >=230,000 and continuing claims are >=1.830 million, indicating a faster transition from low-hire weakness into separations than the model expects.
Initial claims are <200,000 and continuing claims are <1.760 million, indicating both low layoffs and materially faster re-employment than the current low-fire/sticky-duration model expects.
